title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 161
paragraphs: Gelon made these offers, and the Athenian envoy, answering before the Lacedaemonian, replied: “O king of the Syracusans, it was not a leader Greece needed when she sent us to you, but an army. You, however, do not hold out to us any hope that you will send an army, unless you have the leadership of Greece; and you are striving to become commander of the Greek forces. So long as you demanded to be leader of the entire Greek army, it was enough for us Athenians to keep silence, knowing that the Lacedaemonian could answer for us both. But now, since, rebuffed from the demand for the whole, you are asking to command the naval force, we tell you this: not even if the Lacedaemonian allows it will we permit you to command the fleet. This at least is our own right, if the Lacedaemonians do not themselves desire it. If they wish to be leaders, we do not contest it with them; but no one else shall we permit to command the ships. For then to no purpose would we possess a naval force larger than that of any other Greek people, if, being Athenians, we should yield the leadership to Syracusans — we, who boast of a race the most ancient of all, the only Greeks never to have migrated from one land to another, and who had a man whom Homer the epic poet said was the best of all who came to Ilium in drawing up an army and arranging it in battle order. So we are not justly to be reproached if we say these things.”
